Mycronic.why: Its Global Technologies division sells die bonders used to package optical components into transceivers to customers such as InnoLight and Lumentum; division orders rose 176% in Q2 2026 on AI-infrastructure demand.
Mycronic.evidence: Mycronic Q2 FY2026 (07-14-2026), CEO: 'it is really about the optical, very much on the packaging of optical components into transceivers ... Typical customers are, of course, like InnoLight, Lumentum.'

players.product: MRSI high-precision die bonders for packaging optical components into transceivers (Global Technologies division)

connects_to.relationship: die bonding equipment for optical transceiver packaging

contracts.signal: CEO: die-bonding demand is driven by packaging of optical components into transceivers; 'Typical customers are, of course, like InnoLight, Lumentum, and those kind of people who are building transceivers' - super strong demand impacting die bonding directly with those customers.

connects_to.relationship: die bonding equipment for optical transceiver packaging

contracts.signal: CEO named Lumentum, with InnoLight, as typical customers of Mycronic's die bonding for packaging optical components into transceivers, where demand is super strong.

quarterly_data.signal: Q2 2026 results: record order intake of SEK 2.9 billion, up 119%; net sales SEK 2.4 billion, up 17% (second-best level); gross margin 57%; EBIT SEK 698 million (29%); backlog SEK 5.25 billion. Rolling 12-month sales SEK 8.65 billion with a 26% EBIT margin; record aftermarket revenue SEK 544 million in the quarter, above SEK 2 billion on a rolling 12-month basis (24% of net sales). Cash SEK 2.7 billion, net cash SEK 2.3 billion.
quarterly_data.figure: orders SEK 2.9 billion (+119%); net sales SEK 2.4 billion (+17%); EBIT SEK 698 million (29%); backlog SEK 5.25 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Full-year 2026 net sales outlook raised by SEK 500 million to SEK 9.25 billion. CFO: the increase comes roughly one third each from higher demand in High Volume, higher demand in Global Technologies (in particular AI infrastructure-related products - die bonding and, to some degree, PCB test) and currency.

Global Technologies (die bonding, PCB test): order intake above SEK 1 billion for the first time at SEK 1,111 million, up 176%; sales SEK 700 million (acquisitions Surfix and ETZ contributed SEK 31 million); gross margin 56%; EBIT SEK 250 million (36%); backlog SEK 2.1 billion. CEO: demand is driven by photonics and communication equipment - packaging of optical components into transceivers - and the AI infrastructure build-out also lifts PCB test; AI-related demand is close to all of this division. CFO/CEO: the 36% margin is on the high side and should normalise around 30% within about a year as capacity and capability are built.
quarterly_data.figure: Global Technologies orders SEK 1,111 million (+176%); sales SEK 700 million; EBIT SEK 250 million (36%); backlog SEK 2.1 billion

quarterly_data.signal: CEO: PCB test lead times are more than a year and a half; a factory expansion adding 25% more capacity takes effect toward the end of the year, with the big difference from early next year, while the constrained supply chain is also being improved. Orders carry long lead times and large down payments, so 2027 and the beginning of 2028 'will for sure be good'. CEO: Mycronic is not the bottleneck - complementary equipment has similar or longer lead times.
quarterly_data.figure: PCB test lead time more than 18 months; +25% capacity from end of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Pattern Generators (mask writers): order intake SEK 625 million (+253% against a weak Q2 2025), four SLX orders including a one-off customised SLX priced at almost $30 million; sales SEK 900 million (Cowin DST added SEK 26 million); gross margin 72%; EBIT close to SEK 500 million (53%); backlog SEK 1.7 billion with 13 systems. CEO: display orders are a little lower than normal; semiconductor mask writer demand is holding up surprisingly well in China and similarly outside China; the PG backlog for coming quarters is 'a little bit on the thin side'.
quarterly_data.figure: PG orders SEK 625 million; sales SEK 900 million; EBIT margin 53%; backlog SEK 1.7 billion (13 systems)

quarterly_data.signal: High Volume (dispensing): order intake almost SEK 700 million (+82%); sales SEK 513 million; gross margin 44%; EBIT SEK 68 million (13%); backlog close to SEK 1.2 billion; demand from the Chinese consumer electronics industry plus AI infrastructure, where dispensing solutions are sold for server assembly, heat-dissipation dispensing in communication equipment and final assembly of optical modules (CEO estimate: AI-related applications less than 20% of the division). PCB Assembly Solutions: record order intake SEK 444 million on its two largest orders ever, both from defence; sales SEK 303 million; EBIT minus SEK 44 million including SEK 39 million restructuring; restructuring aims for about 10% EBIT margin by next year at current volumes.
quarterly_data.figure: High Volume orders ~SEK 700 million (+82%); PCB Assembly Solutions orders SEK 444 million, EBIT -SEK 44 million
